foliage_grade_1104._why: VIS-STORMWOOD (4 Nov 2026): CPU judges on nearly every Stormwood row (j1-j4, qj rounds) name 'bright Meadows-style green canopies', 'pale cartoon trunks' and a saturated carpet instead of the board's cool blue-green moss forest. When enabled (vegetation.gd stormwood_foliage_grade), these per-layer material tints replace the shipped ones per model through the variant_retint overlay: canopies go cooler and about a quarter darker, the giant trees' single material (bark and leaves) drops from warm #d8c8ae to cool #9fb0a8, ferns and bushes follow. No placement, bake input, collision or harvest change. OFF until judged.
foliage_grade_1104._why_adjust: qj_foliage (4 Nov): the tint-only grade was flat (both sides identical): crown_canopy's Leaves_NormalTree and the giant trees' Meshy sheet are bright saturated green textures that no multiply tint can cool. These per-material texture adjusts (vegetation.gd _adjusted_texture) desaturate and darken those sheets; storm_canopy and storm_bush already use the shipped desat55 leaf.

_comment: F41 biome look candidate. One fixed-purple rig at every clock hour; the existing Surge presentation supplies phase, rain, flash and aftermath deltas. OFF until matched Medium/High three-judge Bar A >=8.5. No save, collision, scatter or creature-scale changes.

light_pass_1101._why: GPU batch 5 (2 Nov, three code-blind judges): Stormwood dialogue +0.62, locations 5.64 -> 5.99, world inventory +0.19, glass sink +0.17, fights -0.23 mapped; ships ON. Owner priority 1 Nov: judges cite flat light and crushed darks on almost every Stormwood frame and ask for the fixed purple storm sky, copper and glass highlights, a key with rim on creatures, depth fog and fill so subjects read. One switch: the rig sections and materials below merge over this file's own (stormwood_look.gd with_light_pass), `rim` becomes the storm rim light (stronger and cooler than the parked r26 candidate, which was judged on CPU only) and `fill` adds a soft shadowless fill. Sky stays the fixed purple storm; Surge phase deltas still apply on top. Client presentation only; no bake input. OFF until GPU judged. Storm key a3 (GPU G-storm-light-a3, 10 Nov, three code-blind judges, confirming batch): sun #cfc0ff 2.05, ambient 2.2, exposure 1.5, contrast 1.1, rim #c3b6ff 1.25 / specular 0.85; F41#2 +0.73 (3/3), F41#17 +0.09 (2/3), F41#4/#5/#12 flat, no row drops.

storm_light._candidate: r26 storm light (OFF until judged). GPU F41 R verdict, path to 7.5 item 2: every stand is one dark mid-tone with no rim light. A cool, low, shadowless back light from the side opposite the sun puts a lit edge on trunks, creatures and the trainer, and a little more grade contrast separates the layers. Presentation only.

bark_grey_1110._why_on: GPU G-bark-grey-1110 (10 Nov, LANE-SCOUT b89fa5feb, three code-blind judges, confirming batch): all four rows gain on High and Medium, 3/3; Crown Arch +1.19. Trunks no longer read red family.
bark_grey_1110._candidate: F41#17 (LANE-MESHY, 10 Nov 2026; OFF until judged). GPU judges (batch 41, Crown Arch r3): the trunks round the arch read pink to salmon, the red family Team Tether reserves. Two sources: the crown_canopy CommonTree_3 bark texture itself is red (Bark_NormalTree.png mean RGB 140, 88, 67), so its #746b5b tint still renders red-brown; the storm_canopy TwistedTree bark (texture mean 84, 76, 72) under #a8977a lands red above green and goes salmon under the lilac light. This retints both barks (the CommonTree tint is cool because its texture is red; a saturation adjust on that sheet rendered the trunks near-white on CPU, so none is used) so their albedo is a cool grey-brown with red no higher than green. The groves_1110 trees use the same meshes and follow. Presentation only (vegetation.gd presentation retint; the scatter bake is untouched).
